name: theme-media-references-decisions
body:
source: user feature request "let theme CSS reference the library's shared media/ directory" — theme stylesheets can only use url() to reach files inside their own theme directory, so several themes cannot share one set of brand fonts (EY Gothic / EY Interstate .woff2) without copying the files + @font-face CSS into every themes/<name>/ or moving the @font-face rules into layouts; the user chose the RESERVED `media:` URL PREFIX (e.g. url('media:fonts/EYInterstate-Regular.woff2')), which kalide rewrites to the served media URL, NOT the "documented stable media URL" alternative.

NEW requirement requirements.requirement.theme-media-references (feature project-templates, contained by requirements.requirement.project-templates): theme.css — and any CSS it @imports from its own theme directory — may reference the resolved library's shared media/ via the reserved `media:` prefix; the path is relative to media/ (no absolute, no `..`), the file must exist, validated exactly like the layout `media` helper; at serve time kalide rewrites every `media:` reference to the served media URL; any other scheme, an absolute path or a `..` stays rejected; a theme reaches only its own dir plus the library media/ tree, never another theme's dir.

AMENDED requirements: template-media, template-language, templates-dir-layout (theme + media bullets), templates-dir-validation (step 6 now covers theme.css AND @import-ed CSS: relative url() in-theme plus media: refs validated like a layout `media` argument; @import followed, bounded and cycle-safe; AC updated), agent-authoring, library-agent-guide (both must document the syntax), agent-guide-drift-check (union check + both guides' scope + AC carry the reserved `media:` token).

AMENDED domain: domain.entity.theme (theme.css may carry media: refs; still cannot reach another theme dir), domain.value.media-asset (also addressed by media: from theme CSS), domain.service.load-template-library (step-6 covers theme CSS + imports), domain.service.template-registry (references include theme CSS refs).

INCONSISTENCIES found and resolved [autonomous]:
(1) the code's isExternalRef (internal/template/loadlibrary.go:538) classifies ANY ref containing ":" as external, so today `media:fonts/x.woff2` is rejected outright as a scheme; the reserved prefix must be carved out BEFORE the generic scheme check while every other scheme (http:, data:, //) stays rejected — recorded in the new requirement and templates-dir-validation step 6.
(2) the request asserts errors are "reported with file and line" / "same validation guarantees as today", but today checkThemeURLs (loadlibrary.go:461) passes line 0 to libraryErrorf, so theme url() errors name the FILE only and carry no line; the explicit AC demands file AND line, so the spec requires theme-CSS reference errors (theme.css and imported CSS) to be file:line-qualified — the plan must compute the reference's line from its offset in the CSS. The existing relative-url() wording was folded into the same file:line-qualified rule for consistency; this is a behaviour improvement over today's file-only error, not a pure "same as today".

SPINE added: contains project-templates → theme-media-references; depends-on theme-media-references → template-media, templates-dir-validation, templates-dir-layout; depends-on agent-guide-drift-check, agent-authoring, library-agent-guide → theme-media-references; drives theme-media-references → domain.entity.theme, domain.service.load-template-library, domain.value.media-asset, domain.service.template-registry. [autonomous, per the project's spine conventions]

RESOLVED feedback-1 (templates-dir-validation) [with user, via implementation review]: the spec did not say what an `@import` target using the reserved `media:` prefix does — the url() matcher (cssURLPattern, loadlibrary.go:456) treats `@import url('media:x.css')` as an ordinary `media:` reference and lets it through, yet imports are only followed inside the theme's own directory and only CSS served from the theme route is rewritten, so the imported file under media/ would be neither validated nor rewritten. Amended templates-dir-validation step 6 (the `@import` target must be a relative path inside the theme's own directory and name an existing file there; both import forms — the quoted string `@import "x.css";` and the `url()` form `@import url("x.css");` — are followed; a reserved-`media:`, or any other scheme, `@import` target is a templates error naming the CSS file and line and is never followed, because the prefix is valid only for a url(…) reference within the served CSS) and its AC (added the `@import url('media:x.css')` / `@import 'media:x.css'` acceptance case). Amended theme-media-references for consistency (import-target sentence + matching AC bullet).
